daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Volatility Rankings with Running Averages
daily_quests.description: Using the ASX 200 historical prices dataset, calculate the 30-day rolling standard deviation of daily returns for each stock. Rank stocks by volatility within each month using RANK() and ROW_NUMBER() window functions. Use a CTE to compute daily returns (close - previous close / previous close), then a second CTE to calculate rolling volatility. Return the top 5 most volatile stocks per month, showing ticker, month, volatility rank, and rolling std dev. Filter for 2025 data only.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning and Aggregation Pipeline
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash data from data.nsw.gov.au (or equivalent CSV export). Write a Python script using pandas to: (1) handle missing values in crash severity, location, and date columns; (2) standardise datetime formats; (3) remove duplicate crash records based on crash ID and timestamp; (4) extract new features (day of week, hour of day from datetime); (5) categorise suburbs into regions; (6) aggregate crash counts by region, severity, and day of week; (7) export the cleaned and aggregated dataset to CSV and JSON formats. Include data quality checks (row counts before/after cleaning, null counts per column) printed to console.

daily_quests.title: Melbourne Pedestrian Traffic Analysis: Trend Detection and Reporting
daily_quests.description: Use the Melbourne pedestrian counting dataset (Melbourne Open Data Portal). Step 1 (Python): Load hourly pedestrian count data, clean missing values using forward fill where appropriate, and create a pandas DataFrame with columns: sensor_id, date, hour, count, day_of_week, is_weekend. Step 2 (SQL): Create a database table from your cleaned CSV. Write SQL queries using LAG() and LEAD() window functions to detect traffic anomalies (hours where count deviates >2 standard deviations from the monthly mean). Use a CTE to compute rolling 7-day average traffic per sensor. Step 3 (Python): Query results back into pandas, generate a summary report showing: top 3 busiest sensors, bottom 3 quietest sensors, and a list of detected anomaly dates/times with explanations (e.g., public holiday, weekend spike). Save report as markdown or JSON.
